_evidence: 0x0040aadb parses a key-frame stream at esi (u16 words): header word +0 (and eax,0x7ff -> count [0x62ac48]; or bp,bp / je 0x40abbe: zero is the CF=1 exit), then tests bp 0x8000 (two words +2/+4 copied to 0x62ac5c/5e), loads cx (the next word), movsx the start word, 0x4000 (shl 16 + one more word), 0x1000 (else shl 3) -> [0x62ac64], 0x2000 (end word(s) the same way, sub start, cdq, idiv ebp=count). The longest path consumes 8 words (header + 2 + cx + 2 + 2 = 16 bytes), so the 0x40-byte buffer is never overrun. The only fault is idiv by count 0, so the header draws 0 (common, the stc exit) or every combination of the four flag bits with counts 1/0x15/0x7ff/0x803(count 3 plus the unused bit 0x800 the caller 0x40abc1 tests); count 0 with a nonzero header only without 0x2000. A positive divisor <= 0x7ff with a sign-extended 32-bit dividend cannot overflow. Words +2..+0x10 are plain i16 (the scalar mix draws 0 often, so the start value [0x62ac64] is zero - the 0x40abab path - for one or, with 0x4000, two zero words, and also covers sign/extreme values for the shl/movsx/idiv). The trailing bytes are random (never read).
